speakers: Christian Derry (head of macro strategy, CFM)
summary: Panel comparing discretionary and systematic macro from manager and allocator views. Conclusions: they share markets and fundamentals but differ in data capacity vs flexibility, convexity is largely trend following mechanics, and allocators hold a few systematic managers while expecting cash plus 3-5%.

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: forecasting strategy is extremely difficult thing to do as a starting point so we really focus on allocating across of bread of strategies high focus on diversification
claims.claim: Forecasting which hedge fund strategy will do best is too hard, so the allocator diversifies across a breadth of strategies.

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: there's a lot of fundamental dispersion for macro strategies to take advantage of and capture
claims.claim: China weak, US exceptionalism and downshifting developed markets create cross-country dispersion that macro strategies can harvest.
claims.testable: partly - dispersion measurable but link to returns assumed

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: probably somewhere in like the cash plus three to five range and that's with with no exposure to Beta
claims.claim: A diversified hedge fund portfolio should return roughly cash plus 3 to 5 percent with no market beta.
claims.indicator: hedge fund portfolio return over cash

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: we always aim for uh double digigit returns
claims.claim: Hedge fund allocators target double-digit absolute returns, with reasonable drawdowns and low equity correlation, because cash rates are high and hedge funds compete with equity rallies and elevated cash.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: the wall of worry is mounting there's massive debts out there mounting deficits a strong dollar bid
claims.claim: Policy changes (tariffs, immigration, tax cuts), high debt and deficits, strong dollar and duration worries create volatility that favors active management.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: geopolitical risk goes both ways elevated risk could be inflationary uh if if geopolitical risk goes away it could be deflationary
claims.claim: Geopolitical risk is two-sided for macro: elevated risk can be inflationary while its removal can be deflationary.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: especially leaning into positively convex strategies that are volatility friendly
claims.claim: In a volatile policy environment allocators should lean into positively convex, volatility-friendly strategies.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: people say Trump is beta dependent he's going to be also looking at you know wealth creation levels of equity markets
claims.claim: Policymakers may react to equity market levels (a Trump equivalent of the Fed put), so the new mantra is do not fight Trump.
claims.indicator: equity market level as policy trigger

correction.issue: Overstates the quote: no 'Fed put' is mentioned. The speaker says the old trader mantra was 'don't fight the Fed', that a new one is 'don't fight Trump', and that Trump is 'beta dependent' (watches equity wealth levels), in parallel with the Fed being data dependent.
correction.fix: Jackie Rosner says the old mantra 'don't fight the Fed' now has a sibling, 'don't fight Trump': the administration is transparent about its aims and 'beta dependent' (sensitive to equity market wealth levels), so large policy-driven market moves are expected.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: the signals come mostly from say fundamentals so you you look at things like fiscal monetary policy
claims.claim: Both discretionary and systematic macro use fundamentals (fiscal, monetary, growth, inflation) plus factors like value, mean reversion and carry; they differ in method.
claims.indicator: fiscal, monetary policy, growth, inflation, value, carry

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: multicolinearity in the world of machine learning doesn't really matter anymore because you can compress data
claims.claim: Quant macro can use many correlated inputs because machine learning compresses data, and uses nonlinear pattern-recognition regressions plus robust portfolio construction.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: if you try to do that I think you take a lot of alpha away from the program
claims.claim: A systematic program has to be rigid, since inserting news (a weekend AI release, tariff comments) manually removes alpha.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: our Quant programs typically run one to two month Horizon maybe three months
claims.claim: Graham quant macro runs on one to two (up to three) month horizons, while discretionary PMs trade week to week.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: to react and if you're a very good micro PM you're going to understand that as a as a potential Alpha signal right
claims.claim: A quant system does not react to a geopolitical accident, while a good discretionary macro PM treats it as an alpha signal, though the PM cannot process as much data as the quant.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: an experienced pilot can't focus on more than seven gauges in an aircraft otherwise the probability of a crash goes up
claims.claim: Humans have a bandwidth limit (like pilots with seven gauges), which limits discretionary macro; systematic processes remove that limit.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: it's usually just a couple ideas every year that generate most of the p&l
claims.claim: Discretionary macro is concentrated: usually a few ideas per year produce most of the P&L.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: all of our strategies effectively have hundreds of these competing ideas uh embedded in the strategies
claims.claim: Systematic strategies search a large idea space and hold hundreds of competing ideas, giving more diversity than discretionary books.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: in the last five years I think more than 50% of our models are essentially relying on these large unstructured data sets
claims.claim: Over 50% of CFM models now use large unstructured alt data (ingesting about five terabytes a day), which few firms can exploit.

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: within both strategies you have a lot of relative value investing and really just trying to capture dispersion more or less
claims.claim: CPPIB uses hedge fund macro to diversify away from security selection into asset selection through relative value and directional trend capture.

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: style exposures to you know more sophisticated versions of carry momentum fundamental momentum
claims.claim: Systematic macro provides style exposures such as carry, momentum and fundamental momentum, whereas discretionary is expected to give more real convexity.

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: that might be only one or two big ideas but if you connect on those in the year you can have a great year
claims.claim: Discretionary macro convexity arrives from one or two big ideas a year, so timing and conviction matter.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: these strategies tend to be positively convex and EV friendly and and tend to capture the right Tales appropriately
claims.claim: Both discretionary and systematic macro tend to be positively convex, vol friendly and capture right tails, trading liquid global markets.
claims.testable: yes - return skew can be measured

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: often in sizable large moves they tend to be very similar and correlated and that's the big distinction
claims.claim: Discretionary and systematic macro have different entry and exit points but become correlated in large market moves.
claims.indicator: correlation of discretionary and systematic macro in tail moves

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: the average future strategy whether it's a trend or non- trend has a sharp much lower maybe something like 0.5 but the systematic managers tend to trade at twice the all than the discretionary manager on average
claims.claim: A good discretionary macro trader has a Sharpe just under 1 while the average systematic strategy has about 0.5 but runs about twice the volatility, so absolute returns end up similar.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: we underwrite the people in the process we want to make sure that the investment process is something that's been tested and repeatable
claims.claim: Manager selection underwrites people and process: require a tested, repeatable process and a proven track record, and do not pay for someone's tuition.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: strategy mix within them whether it's uh Trend and momentum or the non Trend momentum stuff uh the speed of their trading people trade at different speeds and holding periods and also the asset class mix
claims.claim: Systematic managers differ on strategy mix, trading speed, holding period and asset class mix, so outcomes vary by manager.

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: you need definitely you know more than one or two managers for sure but definitely less than 10 because you put too many people too much diversification and you just water down the soup
claims.claim: Hold more than two but fewer than ten systematic managers: too many dilutes returns, a single one gives an idiosyncratic experience (a 30-day commodity manager vs others); concentrate in the best over time.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: this idea of convexity that was brought up I it's interesting because it's really just a mechanical effect so when you Trend follow that's going to emerge
claims.claim: Convexity is a mechanical outcome of trend following, not a separate skill.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: it won't go into production if it correlates with something else right and in Macro for example you'll find many times that it'll correlate with like a cluster of trend following predictors
claims.claim: New macro predictors are rejected if they correlate with existing signals, often a cluster of trend following predictors, because they add no new information.
claims.indicator: correlation of new predictors with trend predictors

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: we're looking for these effects that are inconsistent with luck essentially
claims.claim: Systematic research looks for effects statistically inconsistent with luck.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: with discretionary Traders is like there's sort of like a benchmarking problem you're just measuring them on their p&l
claims.claim: Discretionary traders are measured only on P&L, whereas systematic firms can attribute returns to each embedded idea.

claims.speaker: Unidentified panelist
claims.quote: systematic has to remain systematic and if someone were to override a system then all of a sudden they're a discretionary strategy
claims.claim: Overriding a systematic model makes it discretionary, so labels need discipline.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: we have a committee that I chair basically and it's to deal with non-model risk right so you have these emergent risks could be regulatory changes elections we're talking about deep seek for example
claims.claim: CFM uses a committee for non-model risks (regulation, elections, DeepSeek), since markets are nonstationary and nonlinear.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: we never override signals but on rare occasions we'll put constraints on our risk models and ideally that'll feed back into the system you know you codify the logic
claims.claim: Never override signals, but occasionally constrain risk models and later codify the logic into the system.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: that I think is the the key advantage of the discretionary over every other strategy
claims.claim: The main advantage of discretionary macro is the ability to change view on the fly (big tariff, DeepSeek), which quant data processing cannot do.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: you can have the ability to make interventions that are not about Alpha ever but are about respons
claims.claim: Quant firms run a daily risk meeting to understand system positions; interventions in disruptions are risk responses, never alpha.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: machine learning the less you're going to be able to understand what things are doing
claims.claim: More big data and ML reduces interpretability, so humans must still understand how the system is trading.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: it's just a richer way to compress information on large unstructured data sets so you can get much more context for sentiment signals
claims.claim: LLMs are useful for classification and compressing unstructured data into sentiment signals and for coding.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: we don't like to use unsupervised machine learning I think it has a huge today it's super prone to over Feit so to perform incredibly
claims.claim: Unsupervised ML overfits (strong in sample, poor out of sample), so use ML for alpha discovery and then understand why the alpha exists.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: to discover Alpha then then we can converse and understand why that Alpha is there great Tool
claims.claim: AI is a great tool for discovering alpha, which humans then explain.

claims.speaker: Unidentified panelist
claims.quote: biggest macro risk fiscal trajectory unsustainable
claims.claim: Panelists named unsustainable fiscal trajectory, AI disruption and higher inflation and rates as biggest macro risks.

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: the structure of the firm is very flat uh so we don't have any pods all the researchers collaborate
claims.claim: CFM runs a flat research organisation with no pods: all researchers work on one shared research base whose output propagates to every strategy, so ideas are tested once against a common predictor set rather than inside siloed books.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: 25% is where we have discretionary PMS so we call that the discretionary fund a different way of dealing with the same problematics same markets same issues
claims.claim: Graham runs roughly 70-75% of its assets as quantitative macro and about 25% as discretionary PMs and treats the two as different methods applied to the same markets and the same problems, not as different businesses.
claims.indicator: share of assets in systematic vs discretionary

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: there's a fear of uh China exporting deflation
claims.claim: Part of the early-2025 wall of worry is a fear that China exports deflation, which together with tariffs and a strong dollar adds to cross-market volatility that macro traders can use.
claims.indicator: Chinese export prices / global goods deflation
claims.direction: deflationary pressure on goods prices from China
claims.conditions: weak Chinese domestic demand and strong dollar
claims.testable: partly - China PPI and export price series exist

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: be going up forever so the fact that there is going to be volatility and trading opportunity I think gives investors a chance to be making more than Cash Plus three to five
claims.claim: Because the equity rally cannot continue forever, the coming volatility and trading opportunity should let hedge fund investors earn more than the base case of cash plus 3 to 5 percent.
claims.direction: hedge fund excess return above cash plus 3-5
claims.testable: partly - hedge fund index excess over T-bills in high-vol years

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: all of civilization's data up to 2006 is about 5 exabytes now we create that data every two days
claims.claim: Data volume is growing exponentially (a quoted figure, which the speaker himself says is probably incorrect), so the edge goes to firms with the technology stack and experience to process unstructured data at scale.
claims.conditions: needs large technology investment; few firms qualify

claims.speaker: Nicholas Cormier
claims.quote: both these uh strategies are just trying to diversify across asset classes across Styles and across timing Horizons
claims.claim: The allocator holds discretionary and systematic macro together to diversify along three axes at once: asset classes, styles and timing horizons.
claims.testable: partly - correlation of manager returns by style and horizon

claims.speaker: Jackie Rosner
claims.quote: we like their expertise to be an inch wide a mile deep
claims.claim: In manager selection the allocator prefers specialists whose expertise is narrow but very deep and proven, over generalists.
claims.conditions: applies to discretionary and systematic hiring

claims.speaker: Christian Derry
claims.quote: so we've been using machine learning for TW uh 20 years but the llm is sort of the disruptive technology
claims.claim: Classical machine learning has been used in systematic investing for about 20 years, so the new element is the large language model, which is the genuinely disruptive tool because it handles unstructured text.

claims.speaker: Pablo Calderini
claims.quote: techniques like singular value composition data compression and pattern matching what have you they were there before cosign similarity but now we're using them in a cohesive way
claims.claim: Singular value decomposition, data compression, pattern matching and cosine similarity are old techniques; what is new is that AI now combines them into one coherent pipeline for extracting signals from large data.
